rationale: The candidate is readable as an attempted gym massing, but it fails the gymnasium hard pass because the dominant body is not legible as one usable long-span hall across all views. The four-view set shows several small orange pieces hovering on the parcel rather than one coherent primary mass; in plan and oblique views they read as separated bars and wedges, and some volumes visually overlap or collide rather than forming a unified sectional rule. The parcel is respected in the basic containment sense, but the open-space figure is weak and not convincingly organized as a public threshold tied to the blue access edge. The roof/section language is also underdeveloped for a gym: it does not clearly express span, structure, or daylight, and instead reads as fragmented stepped pieces. The mass has some precedent resonance with low sports bars and courtyard-based facilities, but currently it is closer to a broken composition than a clear hall plus subordinate support bar. The best next correction is to preserve the general low horizontal gesture, simplify to one dominant hall, and carve a more legible access-side void or court while strengthening the section/profile.
